turns.content: Hello, I'm your doctor today. What brings you in today?

Doctor: Hello, I'm your doctor today. What brings you in today? Patient: I’m here for my annual blood pressure visit, and I really don’t have any new complaints—just occasional knee pain from my osteoarthritis.
Patient: No new symptoms from that—my osteoarthritis is just occasional knee pain, and I take acetaminophen only as needed. I’m not having any other issues and my blood pressure has felt stable.
[ASK] Do you have a new or worsening skin lesion that is persistent and non-healing (e.g., scaly/rough or changing spot)?
Patient: No, I haven’t noticed any new or worsening skin spots or lesions, and nothing has been persistent or non-healing. I feel well otherwise, aside from the occasional knee pain I mentioned.

Doctor: Are you experiencing **psoriatic arthritis**? Patient: No, I’m not having symptoms like that—just occasional knee pain related to my osteoarthritis, and I haven’t noticed any skin or joint changes beyond that.
Patient: No, I’m not aware of any chronic kidney problems—I feel well overall and I haven’t had any symptoms like swelling or fatigue.
[ASK] Are you experiencing **chronic obstructive pulmonary disease**?
Patient: No, I don’t have COPD and I’m not having any shortness of breath or chronic cough. I feel well otherwise and my main issue is just occasional knee pain.
Patient: No, I’m not experiencing pneumonia—I don’t have fever, cough, or any breathing issues. I feel well overall aside from my occasional knee pain.
